title: Care Center Training Notes: The Electric Service Agreement Chronic-Outage Credit
content:
These training notes answer the questions the chronic-outage credit rule of the **Electric Service Agreement** settles. The chronic-outage credit compensates repeated interruptions at a service address rather than one long one.

**Which outage records does the chronic outage count take in?**
The count includes every outage record at the address regardless of duration, cause or major event day, because the chronic credit compensates repeated interruptions rather than one long one. A short interruption, a weather or planned maintenance outage, and an outage that began on a declared major event day are each counted.

**How often can an account receive it?**
At most one chronic-outage credit is posted per account in any 12 months, so it is not granted when the account already has one or more chronic-outage credits posted in the 12 calendar months ending on the handling date.

| Chronic-outage credits on the account in the 12 calendar months ending on the handling date (hypothetical) | Granted under this limit? |
|---|---|
| none | not barred by this limit |
| one | no |
| two or more | no |

A chronic-outage credit posted before that 12-month window does not bar a new one.

**Can it be combined with a sustained-outage credit?**
Yes. It stacks with any sustained-outage credit for the same outage record.

**Clauses no longer in force.**
- The clause that granted the schedule's chronic-outage credit amount when the outage count for an outage record reached the schedule's chronic threshold is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.
- The clause that attached the credit to the outage record that reached the threshold and posted it on request under the sustained-outage claim window is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.

superseded_clauses: A chronic-outage credit (credit_code chronic_outage) of the schedule's chronic_outage_credit_usd is granted when service_msr_outages_12m for an outage record reaches chronic_outage_count_threshold.
The credit is attached to the outage record that reached the threshold and is posted on request under the same claim window as the sustained-outage credit.
